newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end sharply up after NCD issue.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end sharply up after NCD issue.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed sharply higher on Tuesday after the central bank on Monday issued T$5 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit despite already tightened liquidity, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 5.816 percent against Monday's 5.473 close, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.75-6.00 percent against 5.50-5.60.

After Monday's NCD issue, the banking system's accumulated reserve excess had become a negative T$158.2 billion, triggering caution that rates may rise if banking institutions are unable to cover such a big excess, dealers said.

Taiwan central bank official Peng Chin-tang said following the market's close on Tuesday that necessary measures to stabilise short-term interest rates would be taken if movements become too volatile. But he added that the bank would not take actions based on single-day movements.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.9150-9200 percent against 5.9180.
